entwurf.thema: ChatGPT Codex Privacy and IP Issues

teile.text: Your AI intern is forging signatures and spying!
teile.name: Drama Hook
teile.szene: A man with black hair and glowing cyan glasses in a black leather jacket stands in a rain-slicked painted alleyway. He looks at a digital tablet showing a cartoon with a forged signature, looking shocked.

teile.text: OpenAI’s Codex desktop app bundles its own LibreOffice.
teile.name: Tool Bundle
teile.szene: A high-resolution capture of the ChatGPT Linux desktop app showing the Codex interface. A file browser sidebar highlights a folder named codex-primary-runtime containing native LibreOffice binary files.

teile.text: Click Create project in Linux to link files. Be sure to like, share and save this video.
teile.name: Practical Step
teile.szene: A close-up of the Linux ChatGPT app window showing a cursor hovering over the 'Create project' button. The presenter then appears in a painted city setting, gesturing toward floating social media icons.

teile.text: But the __obi cookie tracks you across different websites.
teile.name: The Twist
teile.szene: A clean technical table from a security analysis showing the __obi cookie. The columns for 'SameSite=None' and 'Max-Age 1 year' are clearly highlighted, indicating its cross-site tracking capabilities.

teile.text: It links purchases to your account, making that fake BLOPER signature look like your AI intern.
teile.name: IP Issue
teile.szene: A minimalist black-and-white digital cartoon in the New Yorker style. In the bottom corner, the pen name 'BLOPER' is visible in a hand-drawn script. The presenter stands beside it, pointing at the forgery.

entwurf.beschreibung: ChatGPT's Codex app bundles its own software, but tracking risks remain. Learn how the __obi cookie and forged artist signatures affect your privacy and identity.
